rows.q: My dog has ticks How do I remove them safely without leaving the head in?
rows.answer:
Remove ticks as soon as you find them:
- Use fine-tipped tweezers and grip the tick as close to the skin as you can
- Pull straight out with slow, steady pressure. Don't twist or jerk
- Don't use bare hands, matches, heat, nail polish or petroleum jelly
- Don't crush the tick. Drop it in rubbing alcohol, seal it in a bag or wrap it in tape
- Wash the bite area and your hands with soap and water

If small mouthparts stay in the skin, it usually heals on its own.

rows.q: My dog keeps scratching Could it be because of the food he eats?
rows.answer:
I had a dog with a similar condition. A couple of things come to mind:
1) food allergies. What are you feeding him? You should be feeding a high quality (expensive) dog food -- the cheap stuff at walmart is cheap for a reason.

Switch to a grain-free product like NutriSource (what I feed). Try that and see if it gets better.

2) I had a dog that was red on his chest and losing hair. My vet diagnosed a bacterial infection. We bathed him every other day in a special shampoo from the vet, and gave antibiotics for 3 weeks, and that cleared him up -- stopped itching, no more red skin, and hair started to come back. Talk to your vet about this possibility.

3) Could be skin mites; too small to see without a magnifying glass. Your vet should be able to spot these.

4) Could be internal parasites. Worms esp. can rob essential nutrients, which can make the dog ill. This could present as skin irritation.

If your pet may have eaten, licked or touched something harmful, call your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now, even if your pet seems fine. Bring the package or label, and only make your pet vomit if a vet tells you to.

rows.q: My dog ate some grapes Is that something I should take him to the vet for right away?

Many everyday foods, medicines and plants are toxic. Act fast, even if your pet seems fine. Signs can take hours or days.

What to do now:
1. Move your pet away from the source and remove anything left in their mouth, if it's safe to do so.
2. Note what they ate, about how much, and when. Bring the packaging, label or a piece of the plant.
3. Call your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now and tell them you're on your way.
4. If it's on their skin or fur (for example a flea product), wash with mild dish soap and lukewarm water, then rinse well.

Go to a vet now.

rows.q: My cat has fleas What's the safest way to get rid of them in the house too?
rows.answer: A bath with dawn dish soap is the safest and most effective method in my opinion. The lather from the soap drowns the fleas, and contains no medicines that can have side effects. In fact, I would say it's the most effective treatment aside from preventative medicines. As with normal baths, just make sure to be careful not to get water in your kitten's ears, and just lather up the soap for a few minutes. You should start to see the fleas start to wash away. Follow up with a flea comb every day, and another bath when you notice any more fleas showing up after eggs have hatched. Diatomaceous earth is best for killing insects in carpet and upholstery I think. Applying it directly to skin can help reduce the risk of secondary infections.

rows.q: I have a Shih Tzu How often should I bathe that breed?

However, we bathe our German Shepherd twice a month and I haven't experienced anything problematic about it.

As far as the smell goes, it is very natural for a dog to have some smell. It should not bother you.

rows.q: Is it normal for cats to sleep most of the day?
rows.answer: Cats can, and will, sleep for 15 to 20 hours a day, but it's important to realize that it's usually a light doze and not the full-blown deep sleep. They're quite able to spring into action from this dozing state with very little hesitation. They do have deep sleep, which only lasts minutes, but that will happen a variety of times during periods of dozing. Most cats also sleep during the daylight hours, becoming more active in the evening. As they're predators, even after so many centuries of domestication, cats follow that same pattern you see with their larger cousins: spending a lot of time in a light doze conserving their energy for hunting and then using that to start feeding themselves again later.

rows.q: How do I trim my dog's nails safely?

Dogs:
- Trim when the nails touch the ground or click on the floor. For many dogs this is about monthly.
- Cut small bits at a time. On light nails, stop a little short of the pink quick. On dark nails, trim just the very tip.
- Don't forget the dewclaws.

Cats:
- Gently press the toe pad so the claw comes out.
- Snip only the sharp white tip. Avoid the pink part, which has nerves and blood vessels.
- Trim every 2 to 3 weeks. At first, do just one or two claws per session.

If a nail bleeds, press styptic powder or cornstarch on the tip and make sure it stops. If your pet fights or gets upset, stop. Your vet can help.

rows.q: My dog keeps scratching Could it be because of the food he eats?
rows.answer:
Itching is a sign, not a disease. The three main causes are parasites (mainly fleas and mites, which are checked first), skin infections from bacteria, yeast or fungus, and allergies to things like insect bites, food, pollen, mold or dust. Itching only in certain seasons often points to a seasonal allergen.

Itching all year can point to dust mites or food.

What to check at home:
- Look through the coat for fleas or flea dirt, and at the skin for redness, scabs or hair loss
- Note where he scratches. Licking and rubbing of the feet and face is common with allergies and infections

See your vet if the itching lasts more than a few days, or if there is hair loss, scaling, a bad smell, or fluid on the skin.

Please don't give human allergy pills or leftover steroids.

Antihistamines often don't work well in dogs.

- Never put a house or yard product directly on a pet

rows.q: How often should I deworm my ? what about kittens?
rows.answer:
Take your kitten to a vet as soon as you can. Ask where you got her about any vaccines, deworming and food she has had.

- Vet visits: kittens usually see the vet every 3 to 4 weeks until about 6 months old, for shots and parasite treatment.
- Vaccines: the core kitten shots start at about 6 to 8 weeks and are repeated every 3 to 4 weeks until 16 to 20 weeks old.
- Deworming: worms are very common in kittens, so many vets deworm them regularly.
- Testing: a kitten with an unknown history should be tested for FeLV and FIV. Keep her apart from your other cats until the vet has checked her.
- Feeding: use kitten food, given several times a day.
- Litter box: one per cat, plus one extra, kept clean.

rows.q: Can dogs eat grapes? What about raisins?
rows.answer:
No. Grapes and raisins can cause sudden kidney failure in dogs, and even a few can be dangerous for some dogs. There's no safe amount.

If your dog ate grapes or raisins:
- Go to a vet now, even if they seem fine
- Tell the vet how many and when

Safer treats include small pieces of plain cooked chicken, carrot or apple without the seeds.

rows.q: When should my puppy get the anti-rabies shot? Is that required by law?
rows.answer:
Every year. Section 5 of RA 9482 says owners must have their dogs "regularly" vaccinated against rabies. The implementing rules make it clearer: a properly immunized dog is one vaccinated yearly, and LGUs register and vaccinate dogs annually.

The shot must be given by a licensed veterinarian, or by a trained vaccinator under a vet's direct supervision during government mass vaccination drives.

Keep the record of each shot on your dog's vaccination or registration card.

rows.q: My dog has ticks How do I remove them safely without leaving the head in?
rows.answer:
Remove ticks as soon as you find them:
- Use fine-tipped tweezers and grip the tick as close to the skin as you can
- Pull straight out with slow, steady pressure. Don't twist or jerk
- Don't use bare hands, matches, heat, nail polish or petroleum jelly
- Don't crush the tick. Drop it in rubbing alcohol, seal it in a bag or wrap it in tape
- Wash the bite area and your hands with soap and water

If small mouthparts stay in the skin, it usually heals on its own.

Watch the spot for a few days. See your vet if it gets red or swollen, if your dog has many ticks, or if he seems unwell in the weeks after.

rows.q: not eating cat days
rows.answer:
When studying animal husbandry, we were taught that cats, in nature, generally fed on many small meals throughout a 24 hours period. An example being they may catch mice at different points throughout the day and night. They don't have the same circadian rhythms as human beings, or dogs, and, naturally, spend as much time active during the day and night.

From my experience and study, it is best to feed for cat at least three smaller meals a day. If the cat does not have a weight problem, and feeding the cat a balanced diet of high quality cat food, it is unlikely to cause any health issues.

rows.q: My dog keeps scratching Could it be because of the food he eats?
rows.answer:
Itching is a sign, not a disease. The three main causes are parasites (mainly fleas and mites, which are checked first), skin infections from bacteria, yeast or fungus, and allergies to things like insect bites, food, pollen, mold or dust. Itching only in certain seasons often points to a seasonal allergen.

Itching all year can point to dust mites or food.

What to check at home:
- Look through the coat for fleas or flea dirt, and at the skin for redness, scabs or hair loss
- Note where he scratches. Licking and rubbing of the feet and face is common with allergies and infections

See your vet if the itching lasts more than a few days, or if there is hair loss, scaling, a bad smell, or fluid on the skin.

Please don't give human allergy pills or leftover steroids.

Antihistamines often don't help dogs with chronic itchy skin.

rows.q: My dog ate some grapes Is that something I should take him to the vet for right away?
rows.answer:
This sounds like it could be poisoning. Many everyday foods, medicines and plants are toxic. Act fast, even if your pet seems fine. Signs can take hours or days.

What to do now:
- Move your pet away from the source and remove anything left in their mouth, if it's safe to do so.
- Note what they ate, about how much, and when. Bring the packaging, label or a piece of the plant.
- Call your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now and tell them you're on your way.
- If it's on their skin or fur (for example a flea product), wash with mild dish soap and lukewarm water, then rinse well.

Don't:
- Making your pet vomit unless a vet tells you to. It's dangerous with some poisons and if your pet is drowsy.
- Home remedies like salt, milk, oil or hydrogen peroxide.
- Giving any human medicine.

Go to your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now.

rows.q: How often should I deworm my ? And is it the same schedule for an adult cat that stays indoors?
rows.answer:
Parasite experts (CAPC) recommend year-round protection for adult pets. Many monthly preventives cover worms together with heartworm, fleas or ticks.

If your pet isn't on a year-round preventive:
- Deworm about four times a year
- Have a stool (fecal) test 2 to 4 times a year

Even on prevention, healthy adults should have their poop checked at least twice a year. Pets that hunt, roam, travel or mix with many animals may need it more often.

Ask your vet for a product that suits your pet's weight and age, and which worms are common where you live.

rows.q: My cat has fleas What's the safest way to get rid of them in the house too?
rows.answer:
Most of the flea problem lives in your home, not on your pet. Eggs fall off into carpets, bedding and corners, and flea cocoons can wait there for months.

What helps:
- Treat every dog and cat in the home, not just the itchy one, using products your vet recommends
- Vacuum often
- Wash pet bedding and blankets regularly
- If you use a home spray, keep pets out of the room and follow the label
- Never put a house or yard product directly on a pet

Fleas can live indoors all year, so experts advise year-round flea prevention. It can take weeks to months of steady treatment to fully clear an infestation.

rows.q: Can dogs eat chocolate? What happens if he already ate a small piece of it?
rows.answer:
Chocolate is poisonous to dogs, especially dark and baking chocolate. Call or go to a vet now, even if your dog seems fine, because signs can take hours to show.

While you get there:
- Note the type of chocolate, how much, and when it was eaten
- Bring the wrapper if you can
- Don't make your dog vomit unless the vet tells you to

Watch for vomiting, restlessness, fast breathing, shaking or seizures, and tell the vet straightaway if you see them.

rows.q: My dog has ticks Can those make him really sick?
rows.answer: Talk to your veterinarian about the best tick prevention products for your dog and tickborne diseases in your area. Check your dog for ticks every day to further reduce the chances that a tick bite will make your dog sick. This is especially important after they spend time outdoors. If you find a tick on your dog, remove it right away.

rows.q: not eating dog days , dangerous ?
rows.answer:
I'm not sure I have an answer for exactly that. This is the closest one I have, to the question "My dog ate a handful of macadamia nuts from a cookie tin.":

Macadamia nuts can make dogs sick, usually within 12 hours. Signs include weakness, vomiting, wobbling, tremors, fever and low energy. Most dogs get better within 1 to 3 days, but call your vet or the nearest 24-hour clinic now and take him in.

Cookies and nut mixes can also contain chocolate or raisins, which are more dangerous, so tell the vet everything that was in the tin.

Before you go:
- Bring the packaging and estimate how much he ate.
- Only make him vomit if a vet tells you to.

On the way, keep him calm and comfortable, and note any vomiting or shaking.

rows.q: I have a Shih Tzu How often should I bathe that breed?
rows.answer:
Most Shih Tzus do well with a bath every 3 to 4 weeks. Bathing too often can dry out their skin.
- Use a dog shampoo, not human shampoo
- Brush before the bath to remove tangles, then dry them fully, especially the ears
- Wipe the eyes and face daily, as tear stains and food build up there

Many owners keep a short "puppy cut" with a groom every 4 to 6 weeks, which makes daily care much easier.

rows.q: Why is my cat peeing outside the litter box? Could it be a medical problem that needs a vet?
rows.answer:
First, have your vet rule out a medical problem. Peeing outside the box can be a sign of a bladder problem.

Go to the vet now if your cat strains in the box with little or no pee coming out, cries while peeing, or is vomiting or very tired. A blocked bladder can kill, and male cats are most at risk.

If the vet finds nothing wrong, check the box:
- One box per cat, plus one extra
- Scoop daily, and change all the litter weekly
- Most cats like unscented, clumping, fine litter
- Put boxes in quiet spots, away from food bowls and busy areas

Stress, like a move or a new pet, can also cause it. Clean accidents with an enzyme cleaner for pet odors. Never punish your cat.

rows.q: My cat is vomiting a lot, what should I do?
rows.answer:
This sounds like it could be vomiting & diarrhea. One episode in a bright, adult pet is often minor. Call your vet for advice and watch closely for the warning signs below.

What to do now:
- Call your vet and describe what you've seen. A photo helps.
- Offer small amounts of water often.
- If your vet agrees, feed small portions of bland food, like plain boiled chicken and rice for dogs.
- Keep a sick puppy away from other dogs and disinfect the area. Parvovirus spreads easily.

Don't:
- Human anti-diarrhea or stomach medicines. Some are toxic to cats and some dogs.
- Withholding food from a cat for more than a day. It can cause liver disease.

Call your vet for advice.

rows.q: Is it normal for cats to sleep most of the day?
rows.answer: Cats usually sleeps most of the day (I'm not exactly sure about the night). How many hours a day (approximately) is it normal for a cat … A: Cats can, and will, sleep for 15 to 20 hours a day, but it's important to realize that it's usually a light doze and not the full-blown deep sleep. They're quite able to spring into action from this dozing state with very little hesitation. They do have deep sleep, which only lasts minutes, but that will happen a variety of times during periods of dozing. Most cats also sleep during the daylight hours, becoming more active in the evening. As they're predators, even after so many centuries of domestication, cats follow that same pattern you see with their larger cousins: spending a lot of time in a light doze conserving their energy for hunting and then using that until the next feeding opportunity.

rows.q: How do I trim my dog's nails safely?
rows.answer:
Go slowly and keep it positive with treats and praise.

Dogs:
- Trim when the nails touch the ground or click on the floor. For many dogs this is about monthly.
- Cut small bits at a time. On light nails, stop a little short of the pink quick. On dark nails, trim just the very tip.
- Don't forget the dewclaws.

Cats:
- Gently press the toe pad so the claw comes out.
- Snip only the sharp white tip. Avoid the pink part, which has nerves and blood vessels.
- Trim every 2 to 3 weeks. At first, do just one or two claws per session.

If a nail bleeds, press styptic powder or cornstarch on the tip and make sure it stops. If your pet fights or gets upset, stop. Your vet can help.
